excellent sunscreen with skin loving ingredients, broad spectrum, great little container. The "Drop the Bomb" BBOSONG Suns stick uses one of THEE best UVA/UVB sunscreen ingredients on the planet: "Bis-Ethylhexyloxyphenol Methoxyphenyl Triazine"! Say that 5 times fast. Or once. lol. It is a broad spectrum, highly photo stable, chemical sunscreen. Chemical sunscreens mean that they absorb rays and disperse as heat before they can reach skin and do damage. The SPF rating of 50+ and PA++++ means that it offers the highest amount of protection that a sunscreen can offer.

Korean skin care, particularly sunscreens, can use super effective ingredients that products made in (or for) USA can not have because the governing bodies have not approved it. It is not because they are unsafe, but because there is a significant amount of bureaucracy involved. No new sunscreen ingredients have been approved in the USA in over 15 years, sad since there are so many wonderful innovations in the rest of the world. We lag greatly behind. Fortunately, we can still buy these products.

The other sunscreen used in this product is, Ethylhexyl Methoxycinnamate (Octinoxate)- a less stellar chemical sunscreen that has mixed thoughts on its efficacy, safety, and desirability. It protects only against UVB rays and breaks down when exposed to light (10% per 30-40 minutes). However, when combined with another broad spectrum sunscreen, it compliments it very well.

The third sunscreen component is, Octocrylene. Screens out the UVB and somewhat in the UVA II range. It is quite photostable (loses 10% of SPF protection in 95 mins) and is often used to stabilize other photo-unstable UV-filters (octinoxate) It is also often used to improve the water resistance of the products.

Very nice moisturizer. his is a nice moisturizer for men but in my eyes could also be used for women. It is pretty much fragrance free which makes it great for people who are sensitive to fragrances. This was my favorite soap - and I depended on it for the fantastic exfoliation, better than any other I've tried (and I tried a dozen kinds).

All of a sudden, in this last batch, they have simply removed the exfoliation completely. Now, when you look at the website, it says "Important Information: We have recently removed our exfoliating oats and coffee grounds due to customer feedback. Our scent is now 100% essential oils no fragrance oil."

Well, I'm here to give you a 1 star review for this "important information". There are 1,000 other soaps that you can buy with various interesting scents, etc. But this was the only soap you can buy that had great exfoliation.

Hopefully, the 'customer feedback' that caused them to remove the exfoliation will be blasted away by the customer feedback complaining that the exfoliation is missing, and they'll put it back.

The One Cologne describes the scent as "Coriander, Grapefruit, Cardamom seed, Tobacco, Basil, Cedar, Ambre, Ginger, Orange Blossom." Some of those things I have no idea what they smell like, but I'd say this not really a musk based scent but it smells really yummy on Bobby. It takes a little more spray than the original version The One Cologne, however, it's about 1/3 the cost, so I won't complain. It's still pretty strong with a couple of sprays being all he needs. As far as wear, it lasts a long time. It's sensual/manly in it's scent and he said he received several complements on the cologne. It is also a large bottle at 3.3 ounces delivered to the door for under 15.00. We like the cologne and can recommend it.

Another winner from Majestic Pure. I have many Majestic Pure products (from skin care products, to hair care, to essential oils), and have always been very satisfied. I am also pleased with the retinol cream. Having very sensitive skin, I tend to use products containing retinol quite sparingly (aka, every few days, vs. daily) as they tend to cause my skin to become quite irritated or scaly after a few days of daily use. I’ve been using this around just my eyes every evening (about 1 hour after applying a hyaluronic acid serum), as my skin is so sensitive that using anything with retinol on my entire face seems to really cause a lot of scaliness. And, this is where the fine lines are really beginning to show.

The results – after using a cream with retinol in combination with hyaluronic acid serum for 3 weeks, I’ve been noticing a definite reduction in the fine lines. They are still there but they were becoming really noticeable.

The cream has ingredients that are highly moisturizing (again, which I like to follow up on a serum with). The consistency is pretty thin (not thick and creamy like a lotion), and there is no noticeable fragrance. It seems to absorb quickly and is not oily.

Some note on the ingredients:

Retinol 2.5% - Retinol is another name for Vitamin A, which is an antioxidant (helps reverse the damage caused by free radicals, apparent in wrinkles and aging), encourages the production of collagen, and elastin.
Jojoba Oil - closely resembles sebum (a waxy substance produced by our skin glands), packed with vitamins and minerals - Vitamin E, B, copper, zinc, selenium, iodine and chromium.
Green Tea - Tea is high in anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, whether ingested or applied topically. Green tea contains tannins which can reduce puffiness and inflammation of the skin. Wrapped in a Dream. This opens all lilies and bergamot, heady and strong. It dries down quickly to a soft jasmine with a touch of gardenia and a hint of rose, amber, and cedar. The fragrance remains true from drydown until it fades completely, which is a good six hours or more; surprisingly long for eau de toilette.

The sillage is a bit more than moderate. You can keep it closer to yourself by spraying it below the waist. I always wear fragrance below the waist, usually at my knees to allow it to float up rather than away. That way I can enjoy any fragrance I wear without bothering other people.

Not quite a soliflore, but close. It smells almost like jasmine green tea, except that hint of gardenia. I wear it by itself or layer with a woody or rose fragrance. I think jasmine is wearable all year long, and it doesn't belong to a particular age group. This is a quieter fragrance than Tea Rose. It's cheerful yet cozy, and easy to wear.

Because of the generous size and the nature of the fragrance, I sometimes use it as a room or linen spray. Sometimes it's hard to believe something so pleasing and universally appealing can be found for such a small price. Kudos to Perfumer's Workshop for this treasure.

Untouchable summer fragrance, out-of-this-world good. I ordered a number of sample colognes from eBay recently after reading an article about the top rated colognes available on the market. I have never smelled a scent that lit my eyes up like this one did when I first sprayed it. If you're on the fence, you can buy a small sample on eBay for like $8. I would be hard-pressed to find anyone who doesn't love this scent, especially at this very reasonable price.

Supposed to be a somewhat love / hate scent. I loved it from the first sniff.. I bought this because.............

1.) It gets a lot of reviews on YouTube and Lalique seems to get a lot of respect as a company.
2.) It's supposed to be a good example of a Vetiver fragrance
3.) Vetiver seems to be a big category for men's fragrances.
4.) As a newcomer to men's fragrances, I had no idea what Vetiver actually smelled like.
5.) This stuff is widely discounted and it seemed like a low risk option to learn about Vetiver and answer some of my questions.

So how does it smell? Great! I loved it from the first moment of the first spray through the dry down right up until it disappeared on my skin.

Reviewers use words like "dark, brooding, mysterious, and serious" to describe this. I don't get any of that. It just smells good. It makes me happy. No, it's not a light citrus smell for summer days. It's a heavier, richer smell that's probably better for an evening out.

Personally I find this a lot like the Dolce & Gabbana The One EDP I also bought. The smell is totally different but with both these fragrances.........
1.) I just liked the smell from the first moment.
2.) The concentration is Eau De Parfum for both.
3.) The longevity, projection, and sillage seems similar.

And speaking of performance, this is NOT "beast mode" stuff. It's more subtle. And as a newcomer I'm learning that can be a good thing or a bad thing depending on the circumstances when you're wearing it. But for the most part, subtle is safer and understated is the classier way to go. So for both the D&G The One EDP and this Encre Noir A L'Extreme these impress me as grown up fragrances that come off as sophisticated scents for grown men who wear suits for a living. I think this would be out of place on a guy in torn jeans, sneakers, and a tee shirt.

So performance..........

Twice As Much of A Waste As One Bottle!. The current version of Tsar is a pitiful, inert, dullard of a fragrance that smells markedly like Old Spice. No need for anyone save masochists to stockpile!

Per other reviewers considering vintage bottles, this fragrance used to be an interesting powerhouse. Unfortunately, as IFRA (regulatory agency) restrictions on perfume content and overall manufacturing costs have increased, many manufacturers have simply stopped trying to inventively reformulate older fragrances, so what the buyer ends up with is the modern version of Tsar: a weak not especially complex or interesting scent with minimal projection and average longevity. When applied, I get a burst of alcohol and green, and then in about 10 minutes, some hint of pine, amber, and florals (carnation, geranium, lily of the valley maybe?). I smell no leather, no oak moss, no vetiver, no tonka beans, and only the slightest hint of patchouli. This becomes a skin scent really quickly, i.e. no projection, but it does last for about 6-8 hrs as a skin scent. This long duration is really the only major advantage Tsar has over Old Spice, which sells for half the price and smells oddly similar!

On Fragrantica.com, there are like 27 different scent ingredients listed for Tsar (or at least claimed for Tsar by its manufacturer), which is simply absurd. VC&A are either having some fun with us, citing historical formulas that are 10 years put of date, or have succeeded in generating the blandest possible result from the most ornately Byzantine of recipes. In comparison, Terre D'Hermes, with a mere 8 ingredients cited on the same site, smells like it is several magnitudes of complexity higher, a symphony compared to Tsar's hummed nursery rhyme.

Frankly, I think most buyers should spend their dollars elsewhere. Many of the old vintage powerhouses have not been reformulated into the same decreptitude that Tsar has; Azzarro Pour Homme, Lapidus, Aramis, Havana,

What Heaven Smells Like?. My first exposure to English Laundry cologne was a BirchBox sample of Arrogant. The very first time I tried it I loved it and received several compliments. When I hear people describe fragrance as “clean,” it usually means one of three things: 1., it smells like powder or soap, 2., it smells “minty,” or 3., it smells medicinal. “Clean” was the first term that came to mind when I first smelled Arrogant, but it does not at all smell powdery, minty, or medicinal. It’s a very sexy-clean smell, but not at all heavy on the musk.

Two of these fragrances are actually Eau de Parfum (Notting Hill and Oxford Bleu), which is very unusual for men’s fragrance. These have a much higher concentration of essential oils, as opposed to Eau de Toilette. The fragrance really does last all day, and the smell doesn’t deteriorate or change at all. According to an old adage, “if you can smell your own cologne or perfume while you’re wearing it, you’re wearing too much.” At least in the case of English Laundry fragrances, I disagree entirely. You’ll want to smell yourself all day while wearing any one of these four fragrances. So will most everyone else around you. This is packaged very nicely, and both the case and the individual bottles have an expensive look and feel. The only thing I don’t like is the name of my favorite cologne of the set. When someone invariably asks what I’m wearing, I have to say, “Arrogant.” What a douche bag thing to say! Otherwise, perfect.

The opening is very fresh, sharp, bright, inviting, unique, and delectable. The green apple, mint, ambroxan, and lemon are the most prominent opening notes. The lemon is the fresh and bright opening note, astringent, sour, and vibrant; the green apple is by its side, delectable, sweet, sour, crispy, and acidic. The mint rounds up the opening with its cooling green and slightly spicy note. The ambroxan is also noticeable musky, lemony, and ambery note that works well, improving the fragrance's projection. As the fragrance moves towards its dry down, the tonka bean and vanilla add a sweet and aromatic touch without making the fragrance overly sweet or taking the focus away from the mint, green apple, and lemon. The vetiver, oakmoss, and cedar are part of the support notes; they combine their notes to create a fresh green and woody accord but remain in the back of the fragrance. The fragrance is linear, all notes come up as soon as the fragrance is applied and continue into the dry down. Once Grand Parfums Versace Eros has reached its full dry down, it can be summarized as a strong projection, spicy mint, fruity green apple, musky ambroxan, mildly sweet vanilla, tonka, and woody cedar fragrance. The fragrance feels casual, comforting, delectable, energizing, exquisite, fresh, fruity, green, high-quality, inviting, masculine, modern, musky, nicely-blended, playful, refreshing, rich, sharp, seductive, sour, sparkly, special, sweet, unique, versatile, wild, woody, and very pleasant.

For better skin care, you can add one drop of essential oil in the powder and mix well. Then, add distilled water and mix again to form a thick paste. Some good essential oils to use are palmarosa, rose otto, frankincense, lemon, juniper berry, lavender, Melissa, cajeput, cistus, silver fir, or rose geranium. Keep in mind that essential oils are acidic by nature and must be diluted when used for skin care, especially when it comes to facial care. Some good carrier oils are grapeseed, avocado, sweet almond, and fractionated coconut oil. These oils are loaded with therapeutic values. Choose the right one for your skin type. - Noir de Noir: complex, sweet, lovely scent. Not overwhelmingly floral, not overpowering, and not sharp/edgy. This is my husband's favorite when I wear it.

- Vanilla Tobacco

- Amber Absolute: Unique, herbal. Stronger than Noir de Noir. Initially, I couldn't stand Amber Absolute. It smelled to me like Chinese medicine box. But then I am totally in love with it. It is very unusual. It has a very unique dried herb fragrance and very complex. It reminds me of the fragrance in the air in Big Sur, CA or Mono Lake, CA when the flowers and plants are drying in fall. The fragrance is not floral, not particularly sexy or feminine.

- Tuscan leather: couldn't stand it, very leathery.

- Neroli Portofino: didn't like it at all. Just like some reviewers said, it smells like Tide.

Useful for Travel, but Too Many Shortcomings for Everyday. The Philips Norelco 8040X electric shaver is a compact, lightweight unit that can be used dry or wet. In either case, it uses Nivea for Men shaving conditioner to smooth the razor over your face as you shave. Ultimately, it is capable of delivering a good shave, but it has too many drawbacks to recommend for everyday use.

SHAVING PERFORMANCE

Used dry, the 8040X is below average compared to other shavers that I've used (including my five-year-old Norelco which still shaves rings around this one). Its shaving heads are very compact and pivot nicely so you can easily reach all contours of your face and hard-to-reach areas, e.g. under your nose. However, the blades themselves don't do provide a close shave at all. I have a beard that's only moderately thick/stiff, and the 8040X left me feeling like I would have a five-o'clock shadow in minutes.

Used wet in the shower, its performance is much better. This is also when the Cool Skin moisturizer really shines - in fact, it's downright necessary to get the heads to glide over your face when used wet. It has a pleasant scent and does leave the skin on your face feeling refreshed afterward (even if it's also apparent that the "cool" is just from some alcohol in the formula). It certainly won't be the quickest shave that you've ever had, but if you take your time, you can get results that rival even a blade.

USE & MAINTENANCE

The 8040X comes with a cradle for storing it upright and also for charging it. Unfortunately once the razor becomes fully charged, you can't leave it in the cradle without unplugging it - doing so can damage battery life. Plus, the plug for the cradle is gigantic and ugly, so you won't want to leave the cradle on display anyway. I would have preferred a simple direct-cord charge design instead.

Amazing mineral sun block! No whitecast!. I became a fan of this product as soon as I first put it on. First, it's an excellent consistency. Lots of sunscreens are super thick and icky, but this one was more of a medium thickness, and easily blended in to my skin. Importantly, it did not leave a white cast or any white residue! It is my understanding that mineral sunscreens are generally a better, healthier option to chemical sunscreens, which makes me love this product so much more. Oh, and the smell! Lovely hard-milled scented soap, but not green in color. Roger & Gallet is a premier soap and toiletry company which can be counted on to provide a quality product. This lovely green tea-scented soap is no exception. The beautiful sturdy cardboard box comes with three individually-wrapped soaps. It would make an excellent hostess gift.

Although the scent is subtle and lovely, I was a bit disappointed that the soap itself is yellow. It's a pretty soft yellow, but I was rather hoping that it would be green to match my decor. That said, I would purchase this soap again in a heartbeat. Another reviewer mentioned that the green tea scent is particularly nice for both men and women and I would agree. I will also try the lily of the valley as mentioned by another reviewer. It was my mother's favorite flower.

You cannot go wrong with these lovely soaps.

Recommended.

Exceptional Lip Balm. This is an exceptional lip balm. The tube is smaller size than "regular" lip balms so it fits easily in any pockets. It is probably good for men as well, who don't carry purses, being black in color and having such a discreet size, you can barely feel it in a pocket.

Despite the smaller size, there is a lot of lip balm in it. The whole tube is filled with it. The mechanics are outstanding, the bottom cap is turning smooth with the precision of a Swiss watch. It gives you the feeling of elegance and luxury.

The lip balm itself takes effect immediately, you will feel your lips smooth and flexible right away, it is almost an overwhelming sensation in the first couple of seconds. It has a nutty smell and taste, I would actually gladly spread it over bread for breakfast. it feels natural and edible. It reminds me of the freshly made cookies of grandma. It is an exceptional natural lip balm that you cannot believe you just found given all the chemicals out there.

Along with the exceptional lip balm there are other samples from the same awesome company as you can see in the picture.

Great moisturizer!. For years I've been trying to fight my face acne at the young age of 24, and this past year I was on an escapade to determine the best product out there for my skin. I was always jealous of how other people's faces looked so radiantly clean and beautifully free from acne. But now I think I've found the answer! Hydration creams really can be a remedial solution for acne prone skin, especially when your skin is not getting the nutrients it needs. However, this intensive night cream is just about for anyone who has overly dry or acne-prone skin. I've tested several other hydration creams from Burts Bees and Avalon Organics, and I think this is truly a great product. Application of this night cream by Life Essentials is so easy where just a little dab of this stuff really goes a long way. The bottle lasts for about pretty long (depending on your usage) if you use it consistently every night. Once you apply it to your face for the night, your face will stay moisten & hydrated well until the morning and ready for you to start your day. No need for a second application.

Wash your face with your cleanser and apply this cream, and you'll see healthier skin in days! Also for those that are struggling with acne, sometimes a change of habits is in order. I didn't realize this until I forced myself to stop picking at my face, which I saw a rapid improvement in my face in less than a week. So stop picking at your face, wash your face at least 2x as recommended, and, you'll see results that you've been awaiting! This cream has some smell to it, which some people may not like.

Snozzle with Xtava Black Orchid and Conair Infinity Pro. Similar to some of the other reviewers experiences, I find that the SnozzlePro works pretty well for me, but I do have to be very careful and make frequent adjustments -- it sort of exploits design problems with the tools you are using. I used it with a Conair Infinity ProPro and an Xtava Black Orchid.

Pros:
-It definitely fits my Conair Infinity Pro and probably won't have any trouble fitting other hair dryers.
-It's thick enough to be sturdy, but thin enough that I can stretch it onto the hair dryer.
- I don't experience any leaking or weird smells.
-I can use it (carefully) with the Xtava.

Cons:
-It is made of rubber, so when it heats up the rubber becomes more pliable and loose around the diffuser. I would recommend using this with cold air if possible. Unfortunately, my Conair Infinity Pro has a setting for "Cool" that isn't cold enough. So, I find that this works best if I keep my finger on the blue "Cold Shot" button the whole time.
-The Xtava has a very short connection point, so even though the SnozzlePro works pretty well, there's not a ton of space for it to hold on. That's a problem with the Xtava though, not the SnozzlePro. In particular, it seems to detach most at the top of the connection point and it will fall off while I'm using it. I just sort of use it gently and keep an eye on that top part to make sure it isn't slipping out.

Overall, I think the SnozzlePro is a great product that would probably work best with a diffuser with a longer connection point than the Xtava and potentially a hair dryer that has a truly cold setting.
